gaps.sentence: The article was full of ___ information (ACCURATE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'information'
gaps.explanation: The negative adjective 'inaccurate' (in- + accurate) modifies the noun 'information'.

gaps.sentence: In my opinion, that restaurant is ___ — the food is nothing special (RATE).
gaps.explanation: 'Nothing special' shows the restaurant is praised too much: overrated (over- + rated).

gaps.sentence: The train arrived ___ , despite the snow (PUNCTUAL).
gaps.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'arrived': punctually (-ly). 'Punctuality' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: She showed great ___ (PATIENT) with the children.
gaps.hint: noun needed; beware the similar word meaning 'people in hospital'
gaps.explanation: 'Patience' is the noun (show patience); 'patients' are people receiving medical care.

gaps.sentence: The sky began to ___ as the storm approached (DARK).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: darken means to become dark. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The audience was ___ by her performance (CAPTIVE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ate forms the verb: captivate. The passive 'was ... by' needs the past participle 'captivated'.

gaps.sentence: It is almost ___ to park in the city centre (POSSIBLE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — parking is extremely difficult
gaps.explanation: The in- of 'possible' becomes im- before p: impossible. The context shows a negative meaning.
